# AccessDevOps Blog

> Practical, opinionated field notes on S3-compatible object storage, cloud infrastructure and DevOps — written by the team behind S3 Explorer.

## About
- Author: Clement Baranger — https://cbarange.com
- Company: AccessDevOps — https://accessdevops.com
- Product: S3 Explorer, a desktop S3 client — https://s3explorer.accessdevops.com

## Topics covered
- S3-compatible object storage: AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, MinIO, Backblaze B2, Wasabi
- S3 clients and tooling comparisons
- Cloud infrastructure and cost engineering
- DevOps practices, automation and CI/CD

## Articles
- [Multipart upload: the 5 MiB floor and the 10,000-part ceiling](https://blog.accessdevops.com/blog/multipart-5mb-floor-10000-parts): measures both limits on a running S3 endpoint — the 5 MiB part floor is refused at CompleteMultipartUpload after every byte is sent, part 10 001 fails during the upload — and shows the part-size arithmetic that caps objects at 48.8 TiB.
- [Presigned URLs leak into logs, referrers and chat](https://blog.accessdevops.com/blog/presigned-url-leakage): measures what a presigned URL actually contains (334 characters, 1 009 with a session token), then traces the copies in access logs, CDN logs, TLS proxies and link previews, and shows that the standard signature redaction leaves the key id, date and expiry readable.
- [Object tags or prefixes: which access model survives growth](https://blog.accessdevops.com/blog/abac-object-tags-vs-prefix-policies): separates what a prefix can decide (what a principal lists) from what an object tag can decide (what it reads), with the 20 KB policy wall, tag prices and the two AWS operations where the tag condition does nothing.
- [Chained AssumeRole sessions stop at one hour, silently](https://blog.accessdevops.com/blog/assumerole-chaining-one-hour-ceiling): traces why a role that assumes another role gets 3600 seconds whatever its MaxSessionDuration says, the exact ValidationError, and the batch job that dies mid-run.
- [Presigned POST: cap size and type before the upload starts](https://blog.accessdevops.com/blog/presigned-post-enforce-size-content-type): signs a policy instead of a URL so the bucket caps upload size and content type itself, with the exact error each failed condition returns.
- [Presigned URLs expire at seven days. Then what?](https://blog.accessdevops.com/blog/presigned-url-seven-day-ceiling): traces the 604 800-second SigV4 signing-key ceiling, the three other clocks that kill a link early, and the mint-on-demand pattern that replaces long-lived URLs.
- [When two policies allow and the request still fails](https://blog.accessdevops.com/blog/bucket-policy-allow-still-denied): the five-gate IAM evaluation order that explains why S3 returns AccessDenied when both policies say Allow, and where the hidden deny lives.
- [S3 Explorer walkthrough: zero to browsing in 5 minutes](https://blog.accessdevops.com/blog/s3-explorer-walkthrough): a real session against a local S3 endpoint — provider presets, connection test, bucket browsing, object metadata and the request-metrics dashboard.
- [The real cost of S3: 8 providers compared, egress included](https://blog.accessdevops.com/blog/s3-total-cost-of-ownership): storage, egress, requests and replication modelled across four workloads, with five charts and a reproducible script.
- [Why we started writing about S3](https://blog.accessdevops.com/blog/welcome): most object-storage advice is either outdated or written for a different scale.
